raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

This PR reduces pipeline-parallel communication overhead for decoder models whose
intermediate tensors contain both `hidden_states` and `residual`.

For fused residual + RMSNorm decoder layers, `hidden_states` and `residual` can
have the same shape and are both propagated across PP boundaries. This increases
the amount of tensor data transferred between adjacent PP stages.

This PR adds `IntermediateTensors.consolidate_residual()` to fold `residual` into
`hidden_states` before intermediate tensors leave a PP stage. On the receiving
stage, a zero residual tensor is materialized locally to preserve the expected
`IntermediateTensors` structure for model execution, `torch.compile`, and CUDA
graph paths.

The optimization is enabled by default. The previous behavior can be restored
with:

```bash
VLLM_PP_DISABLE_RESIDUAL_CONSOLIDATION=1
```

Main changes:

- Add `IntermediateTensors.consolidate_residual()`.
- Consolidate residual tensors before PP send.
- Materialize zero residual tensors on PP receive when residual consolidation is used.
- Apply the same behavior in CUDA graph and V2 model runner paths.
- Skip non-tensor values when marking dynamic dimensions on `IntermediateTensors`.
- Add `VLLM_PP_DISABLE_RESIDUAL_CONSOLIDATION`.

## Test Plan

I tested PP serving with the OpenAI-compatible server and `vllm bench serve`.

Benchmark configuration:

- Model: local checkpoint of `GLM-4-9B-0414`
- Pipeline parallel size: 2
- Max model length: 32768
- Prefix caching: disabled
- Dataset: random
- Number of prompts: 64
- Output length: 16
- Input lengths: 4096, 8192, 16384
- Tested both:
  - default behavior: residual consolidation enabled
  - fallback behavior: `VLLM_PP_DISABLE_RESIDUAL_CONSOLIDATION=1`

The benchmark was run with socket-only NCCL communication to make PP-boundary
communication more visible in the end-to-end serving benchmark.

Server command:

```bash
python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
  --model /root/share/models/GLM-4-9B-0414 \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \
  --port 8123 \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching
```

Fallback server command:

```bash
VLLM_PP_DISABLE_RESIDUAL_CONSOLIDATION=1 \
python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
  --model /root/share/models/GLM-4-9B-0414 \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \
  --port 8123 \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching
```

Benchmark command:

```bash
python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench serve \
  --backend openai \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8123 \
  --model /root/share/models/GLM-4-9B-0414 \
  --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len <INPUT_LEN> \
  --random-output-len 16 \
  --num-prompts 64 \
  --save-result
```

## Test Result

PP serving completed successfully with both residual consolidation enabled and
disabled.

Correctness / stability:

- Default path completed successfully.
- Fallback path with `VLLM_PP_DISABLE_RESIDUAL_CONSOLIDATION=1` completed successfully.
- All benchmark cases finished with 64 successful requests and 0 failed requests.
- The receiving PP stage materializes a zero residual tensor locally, so model
  execution does not observe a `None` residual.

Performance result:

| Model | PP size | Input len | Output len | Requests | Residual consolidation | Request throughput | Mean TTFT | Mean TPOT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GLM-4-9B-0414 | 2 | 4096 | 16 | 64 | Disabled | 2.71 req/s | 12904.99 ms | 511.81 ms |
| GLM-4-9B-0414 | 2 | 4096 | 16 | 64 | Enabled | 2.77 req/s | 12696.05 ms | 499.85 ms |
| GLM-4-9B-0414 | 2 | 8192 | 16 | 64 | Disabled | 1.33 req/s | 24943.91 ms | 646.93 ms |
| GLM-4-9B-0414 | 2 | 8192 | 16 | 64 | Enabled | 1.35 req/s | 24463.19 ms | 634.65 ms |
| GLM-4-9B-0414 | 2 | 16384 | 16 | 64 | Disabled | 0.58 req/s | 56697.76 ms | 811.76 ms |
| GLM-4-9B-0414 | 2 | 16384 | 16 | 64 | Enabled | 0.59 req/s | 55783.31 ms | 798.19 ms |

Summary:

| Input len | Throughput change | Mean TTFT change | Mean TPOT change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4096 | +2.2% | -1.6% | -2.3% |
| 8192 | +1.5% | -1.9% | -1.9% |
| 16384 | +1.7% | -1.6% | -1.7% |

In this socket-only PP benchmark, residual consolidation gives a small
end-to-end throughput improvement and slightly reduces mean TTFT / TPOT across
the tested long-context configurations. The end-to-end gain depends on the
communication/computation ratio and the hardware topology.

## Documentation

This PR adds a new environment variable:

```bash
VLLM_PP_DISABLE_RESIDUAL_CONSOLIDATION
```

No model-specific documentation update is required.

## AI assistance disclosure

Parts of this PR were developed with AI-assisted coding tools. I reviewed the
changed code and validated the behavior with the tests listed above.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

## Code Review

This pull request implements residual consolidation for Pipeline Parallelism to reduce communication overhead by merging the residual tensor into hidden states before transmission. The review feedback identifies that setting tensor values to None during consolidation could cause failures in existing IntermediateTensors methods like __getitem__ and empty_like. Furthermore, it is recommended to zero only the active slice of the persistent buffer when handling consolidated tensors to ensure consistency with sequence parallelism logic.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Setting `self.tensors["residual"] = None` breaks several existing methods in `IntermediateTensors` that expect all values in `self.tensors` to be `torch.Tensor` objects. Specifically, `__getitem__` (when using a slice), `__eq__`, and `empty_like` will all crash with a `TypeError` or `AttributeError` when encountering a `None` value. While `torch.compile` paths are updated in this PR, other parts of the codebase or tests using these methods on consolidated tensors will fail. Please update these methods to handle `None` values gracefully.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Zeroing the entire persistent buffer for `k` might be incorrect if `is_rs` (residual scattered for sequence parallelism) is true. In the scattered case, each rank only owns a slice of the residual tensor. While zeroing the whole buffer is safe if it's rank-local, it's inconsistent with the `copy_` logic below which only operates on `copy_len`. It would be better to zero only the active slice `[:copy_len]` to maintain consistency and avoid unnecessary operations on padded regions.

```suggestion
                    self.intermediate_tensors[k][:copy_len].zero_()
```

+        right before the tensors leave the current PP stage to merge the
+        residual and avoid transmitting it.
+
+        ``hs = hs + res`` creates a new tensor — the persistent CUDA graph
+        buffer (if any) is not modified.
+        """
+        hs = self.tensors.get("hidden_states")
+        res = self.tensors.get("residual")
+        if hs is not None and res is not None and res.numel() > 0:
+            self.tensors["hidden_states"] = hs + res
+            self.tensors["residual"] = None  # type: ignore[assignment]

Zeroing the entire persistent buffer for `k` might be incorrect if `is_rs` (residual scattered for sequence parallelism) is true. In the scattered case, each rank only owns a slice of the residual tensor. While zeroing the whole buffer is safe if it's rank-local, it's inconsistent with the `copy_` logic below which only operates on `copy_len`. It would be better to zero only the active slice `[:copy_len]` to maintain consistency and avoid unnecessary operations on padded regions.

```suggestion
                    self.intermediate_tensors[k][:copy_len].zero_()
```

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

## Code Review

This pull request implements residual consolidation for Pipeline Parallelism to reduce communication overhead by merging the residual tensor into hidden states before transmission. The review feedback identifies that setting tensor values to None during consolidation could cause failures in existing IntermediateTensors methods like __getitem__ and empty_like. Furthermore, it is recommended to zero only the active slice of the persistent buffer when handling consolidated tensors to ensure consistency with sequence parallelism logic.
